work.name: Aziro (formerly MSys Technologies)
work.summary: Sole engineer on the account. Python throughout, scoping to handover.
highlights: Sole engineer on an enterprise client account, owning scoping, HLD/LLD, build, test, documentation and handover.

Raised Top-1 accuracy of a two-stage visual retrieval system from 41.9% to 97.7% by growing the feature-based reranker from 3 to 8 features and tuning it against MRR, with CLIP ViT-B/16 embeddings in Qdrant handling recall.
Delivered a config-driven Python desktop CAD validation platform end to end, with DXF parsing, 2D computational geometry, PySide6 and a JSON rule engine, automating 3+ manual workflows.

Built floor-plan variations that move doors and windows and heal the 2D geometry by rebuilding walls and rooms, integrated a client system into the app, and agreed changes and new configurations directly with the client.

Built a server-authoritative economy in server-side JavaScript on Unity Cloud Code for shop, assets and upgrades.
Architected real-time multiplayer and friend challenges on Unity Matchmaker, Lobby and Relay, and a master-follower physics simulation that handles race conditions on nearly every action.

work.name: Zenoti
work.summary: Backend and full-stack work on a large multi-tenant enterprise product.
highlights: Became primary code reviewer within a year, requesting changes on 25+ of 50+ PRs including work approved by senior staff, and flagged 40+ changes that would have become defects.

Designed and owned a localization abstraction layer for a 500+ page C# and ASP.NET product, with providers switchable by configuration, per-element opt-out and coverage through the API and database layers.
Delivered 5 client-specific and 2 core features end to end, and 2 of them were adopted into the core product.
Restored SQL queries degraded 2 to 3x to near-baseline response times with no downtime on a live system.
Removed a data-loss risk by rewriting legacy stored procedures, one of them 4,000 lines, to use differential updates.

projects.name: Portfolio

awards.title: HackerRank Orchestrate, September 2026: rank 224 of 3,062 (top 8%) in a 24-hour AI agent hackathon
awards.summary: HackerRank's 24-hour challenge asked for an AI agent that decides whether someone can safely afford a purchase, scored across 250 requests. The submission combined a deterministic 90-day cash-flow engine, including a verifier that re-simulated every recommendation, with Claude reading 16 receipts and payslips and classifying 215 messages in two languages. Eight tagged versions each tested one hypothesis against 25 solved examples. Model cost for the full run was about $3.
